risk_reasons: Changes three customer-facing and admin-facing email send paths in worker/jobs/, which invariant #1 places on the Railway worker.
Changes src/lib/approval/create-link.ts, shared approval-link code governed by invariant #5 and the approval-security skill.
A wrong 409 classification either drops a real email or re-sends a delivered one; both are silent to the owner.
goal: A crash between the Resend send and the local sent-marker in OnboardingDripWorker and EngagementAlertWorker no longer delivers a second copy of the same email, and the approval link carried by the first copy stays usable.
non_goals: Using a provider idempotency key on a send whose body can differ between attempts. The signed-off intake originally chose the key for all three sites; review proved that breaks hard-bounce correlation, so the day_7 drip and the owner nudge use mark-before-send instead and the owner re-approved that reversal.
Changing the partner satisfaction alert branch (handleSatisfactionAlert). It already marks the Outbox job completed before sending, so a key adds nothing there.
Adding an outbox reference column to notification_deliveries. That is a migration and rides its own PR.
Making sendInternalEmail require an idempotency key, or adding a CI audit that forces one on new call sites.
Changing the two approval-link call sites outside this ticket (worker/jobs/notification/dispatch.ts, worker/jobs/pending-post-notice/dispatch.ts). Their revoke behaviour stays exactly as it is.
Changing the Drip staleness cap, the onboarding_drip_log claim protocol, or the EngagementMonitorPoller cooldown guards.

Fixing AdminExceptionWorker.ts:138-150, which review found carries the identical send-then-mark defect with a guard at :114 that can never fire. Filed separately; it is an internal admin alert and sits outside this edit surface.
Fixing worker/ingress/resend.ts:284, the same no-key shape on the hard-bounce admin alert. Third-party ingress, filed with the above.

Carrying a durable delivery identity to Resend as a tag and reconciling it in the webhook. That would let a body-differing send keep both no-email-loss AND bounce correlation, but it changes ingress and the webhook contract, so mark-before-send is used instead.
user_visible_behavior: A business owner whose day_1 or day_30 onboarding drip crashes after Resend accepted the email receives exactly one copy, not two, and loses no email.
A business owner whose day_7 drip crashes after Resend accepted the email receives exactly one copy, not two. That drip is not re-sent, so in this narrow window it is lost rather than duplicated.

A business owner whose owner nudge crashes after Resend accepted the email receives exactly one copy, not two. That nudge is lost rather than duplicated, and the poller re-nudges after the 3-day cooldown.
The admin inbox receives exactly one partner engagement, escalation, or low-engagement alert per occurrence, not two.

Hard-bounce suppression keeps working for every send in scope: no delivery row carries a synthetic message id on a path where the body can differ between attempts, so worker/ingress/resend.ts can still correlate the bounce and set businesses.owner_email_bounced.

Operators can tell a suppressed duplicate from a genuine send: the notification_deliveries row for a suppressed duplicate carries external_message_id prefixed 'idempotent-replay:', and the worker logs a matching line.
invariants: #5 Approval tokens never stored raw. createApprovalLink is byte-identical to main in the final diff — the revokeMode union is untouched.
#2 The Outbox job stays the unit of work. No send site writes Postgres and separately enqueues BullMQ.
#12 Entry points orchestrate; modules own failure behavior. The Resend 409 classification lives in sendInternalEmail, not in either worker.
#10 Node.js native crypto only. No new hashing, no crypto-js.
#11 The subscription guard ordering in both workers is untouched.
Hard-bounce suppression keeps working: no send that can vary its body between attempts carries a key, so no delivery row on such a path holds a synthetic message id.
A handler that completes its Outbox job BEFORE sending must not rethrow a send failure — BullMQ would retry the job and re-send. The owner nudge swallows and logs, as WeeklySummaryWorker does.

Every provider key in this change is domain-scoped. That matches the MAJORITY of pre-existing house keys, not all of them: NotificationFailoverPoller scopes three to a per-attempt claim id and src/lib/account-offboarding/email-dedup.ts is a named key-builder helper. An earlier version of this invariant claimed all seven were domain-scoped and that no helper precedent existed; review disproved both.

A send that commits its dedupe marker BEFORE calling Resend must leave a durable failure record when the send throws — otherwise the job ledger reports success for mail that never went out. day_7 writes markOutboxFailed; the owner nudge writes insertFailedDelivery, because its outbox row is already completed and markOutboxFailed would no-op.

Both new failure-record writes are best-effort and carry their own try/catch, per .claude/rules/worker-layout.md. An unguarded rejection would escape the handler, BullMQ would retry, and the retry would re-open the exact duplicate each catch exists to close. Both guards are mutation-verified.
edge_cases: A send whose body can DIFFER between attempts must never carry a provider key. Resend answers 409 instead of replaying the original response, so the delivery row would hold a synthetic id, and worker/ingress/resend.ts correlates bounce/delivered/complained ONLY on the real Resend id — a hard bounce would match no row and leave businesses.owner_email_bounced unset. The day_7 drip and the owner nudge are exactly this case (createApprovalLink mints a fresh token per call), so they mark before sending and carry no key. Found by three review axes independently; an earlier cut of this branch shipped the key on both and introduced that regression.

Named residual: day_30 reads its stats per attempt, so a review landing mid-retry changes its body and puts it on the 409 path. That needs a crash AND a same-window stats change. Accepted, not defended.
Resend returns 'invalid_idempotent_request' (409): the same key was submitted with a different body, which proves Resend already accepted the first email. Treat as a successful send.

A replay whose body is IDENTICAL never reaches 409 at all — Resend replays the original 2xx with the original message id. That is the common case for day_1, day_30 and the partner alerts, so it produces no replay flag, no log line and no 'idempotent-replay:' row. The operator query therefore counts body-differing replays only, which is a floor and not a total.
Resend returns 'concurrent_idempotent_requests' (409): the first request is still in flight, which is NOT proof of acceptance. Throw, so BullMQ retries later.
Resend returns 'invalid_idempotency_key': the key we built is malformed. Throw. This is a programming error, not a delivery outcome.
Mock mode (MOCK_EXTERNAL_APIS=true) returns early in sendInternalEmail before any Resend call, so no key is sent and no 409 can occur. Behaviour is unchanged.

The onboarding drip stale-claim takeover (OnboardingDripWorker.ts:227-236) lets a SECOND outbox row take over a claim left with sent_at IS NULL. Two rows carry two outbox ids, so the drip key is scoped to (business_id, drip_type) instead, matching onboarding_drip_log UNIQUE(business_id, drip_type).
An idempotent replay yields no Resend message id. recordNotificationDelivery still requires a string, so the replay records 'idempotent-replay:<key>'.
An owner nudge with zero pending reviews returns before any send, so it never builds a key.

A Resend idempotency key expires after 24 hours. Review disproved the earlier claim that every retry path here completes in minutes: watchdog reclaim x max_attempts plus the scheduler re-mint can exceed the window, after which a duplicate is no longer suppressed. The key is a bound on the crash-retry window, never a durable guarantee.

Every key in this change is DOMAIN-scoped ((business_id, drip_type) or (alert_type, business_id)), matching the house precedent. An earlier cut used the outbox row id for the nudge and partner alerts on the theory that a recurring alert has no domain identity; review disproved it — EngagementMonitorPoller cooldowns are 3/7/14 DAYS, far beyond the 24h key life, so no legitimate second alert can collide, and the domain scope additionally covers the poller re-mint path that an outbox-scoped key misses.

rollback_plan: Revert the single squash-merged commit. No migration, no schema change, no feature flag, no env var. Reverting restores the pre-change send order and the orphaned_only revoke behaviour at both approval-link call sites; the only lasting trace is the 'idempotent-replay:' prefix on any notification_deliveries rows written while the change was live, which is inert data.
observability: notification_deliveries.external_message_id LIKE 'idempotent-replay:%' counts suppressed duplicates whose body differed. It is a FLOOR, not a total: an identical-body replay returns Resend's original 2xx and is indistinguishable from a first send.
The drip and partner-alert handlers each log a line naming the business on a replay. Both lines have a test, and both mutants were verified to fail their test.

A day_7 send that fails after its mark leaves job_outbox.status='failed' with last_error prefixed 'send failed after mark:'. That is the signal for the permanently-lost case, and it exists BECAUSE the handler no longer completes the row. The Job-failure sink does NOT fire on this path — the handler returns rather than rethrowing — so the outbox row is the record.

An owner-nudge send failure leaves a notification_deliveries row with failed_at set, template 'owner_nudge' and failure_reason carrying the provider error. The cooldown probe keys on sent_at IS NOT NULL, so this row does not delay the next nudge.

A day_7 drip lost to a crash (as opposed to a send error) is visible as an onboarding_drip_log row with sent_at set and no matching notification_deliveries row. This table is drip-only; the nudge's equivalent is the failed delivery row above.
